root_cause.text: `l2cap_sock_ready_cb()` in the Bluetooth L2CAP socket layer dereferences `chan->data` as a `struct sock *` without verifying it is non-NULL, so a ready callback can reach `lock_sock(sk)` on a null socket pointer and trigger a null-ptr-deref.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (!sk) return;` immediately after `struct sock *sk = chan->data;` in `net/bluetooth/l2cap_sock.c`, and the CVE/trace shows the crash occurs in `l2cap_sock_ready_cb` at `lock_sock_nested()` during `l2cap_info_timeout`, confirming `sk` was NULL when the callback ran.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (!sk) return;` immediately after `struct sock *sk = chan->data;` in `net/bluetooth/l2cap_sock.c`, and the CVE/trace shows the crash occurs in `l2cap_sock_ready_cb` at `lock_sock_nested()` during `l2cap_info_timeout`, confirming `sk` was NULL when the callback ran.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a null check in the L2CAP ready callback to prevent a crash when the channel has no associated socket.
intent_record.what: The function `l2cap_sock_ready_cb(struct l2cap_chan *chan)` was updated to add a null check for `sk` immediately after `struct sock *sk = chan->data;`. If `sk` is `NULL`, the function now returns early before calling `lock_sock(sk)` or accessing `bt_sk(sk)->parent`.
intent_record.how: This prevents the callback from dereferencing a null socket pointer when `chan->data` has not been set or is otherwise invalid, avoiding a potential kernel crash in this path.

grouping_result.intent: Add a null check in the L2CAP ready callback to prevent a crash when the channel has no associated socket.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it adds a null check in l2cap_sock_ready_cb() before using chan->data as a struct sock *, preventing the null-pointer dereference in lock_sock(sk).

candidates.rationale: This dereferences the channel's data into a socket pointer without any prior null validation. If chan->data is NULL, subsequent use of sk leads directly to a null-ptr-deref.
This is the immediate crash point when sk is NULL, because the callback can reach lock_sock() with a null socket pointer due to the missing check.
This also assumes sk is valid and dereferences it. If sk is NULL, this line will crash as part of the same missing-null-check bug.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line assigns chan->data to sk without verifying it is non-NULL. The root cause is that l2cap_sock_ready_cb() later treats this as a valid struct sock pointer, so a NULL chan->data can propagate into a null-ptr-deref.
This is the immediate crash point when sk is NULL. Because the callback lacks a prior NULL check on chan->data/sk, execution can reach lock_sock() with a null socket pointer and dereference it.
This statement dereferences sk as a Bluetooth socket structure. If chan->data was NULL and sk is invalid, this dereference can also trigger the same null-ptr-deref in the ready callback.
